summary: Bhagavan Das (1869–1958) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his M.A. at the University of Calcutta (~1886–1887). He served at Central Hindu College (~1899–1914) and later as headmaster of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1921–1926).
Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1976), serving as head of its Research Department (attested 1989).

Bhagwan Dash (1934–2015) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi (Ph.D. 1978). He worked as a bibliographer and cataloguer at the Library of Congress.

Bhagwanlal Indraji (1839–1888) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University (~1884). He held posts at the Royal Asiatic Society (1877), the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1877–1888), and the University of Mumbai (1882).

Bhajagobinda Ghosh was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 1994, he was attested as an Editorial Board Member for the Bulletin of Tibetology and Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University, Agra. He held posts at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan (1991).

Bhaskar Anand Saletore (1900–1963) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Henry Heras and doctoral supervisor Lionel David Barnett. In 1936, he was Professor of History at Sir Parashurambhau College.
Bhau Daji (1822–1874) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He completed his studies at Elphinstone College and Grant Medical College (~1845–1851).

Bhikkhu Anālayo works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Peradeniya (Ph.D. 2000) and University of Marburg (Habilitation 2006). He held posts at the University of Hamburg, Dharma Drum Institute, and Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy.

Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Claremont Graduate University (Ph.D. 1972). He served as Editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and president of the Buddhist Association of the United States (2013).

Bhikkhu Pāsādika is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Magadh University and Punjabi University (Ph.D. 1974). His posts include Punjabi University (1975–1977), University of Marburg (1995–2007), and Linh Son Buddhist Academy (2016).
Bhikkhu U Dhammissara is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under supervisor Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe.

Bhogilal Sandesara (1917–1995) worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh. He served at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1951–1975) and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (~1958–1975).

Bhuwan Lal Joshi (1930–1977) was an Indology scholar who studied at Patna University. He held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley, and the University of California, Santa Cruz (~1967–1977).

Bidia Dandaron (1914–1974) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Saint Petersburg State University and under Andrei Vostrikov. He held posts at the Buryat Institute of Social Sciences (1956) and the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies (1957).

Bihani Sarkar is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who held a post at the University of Hamburg and serves as Senior Lecturer in Comparative Non-Western Thought at Lancaster University (attested 2026).

Bill M. Mak works in Indology and history/archaeology. He held appointments at Kyoto University (2014–2019), the Needham Research Institute (2019), the University of Science and Technology of China (2024), and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Bimal Krishna Matilal (1935–1991) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Calcutta, Sanskrit College, and Harvard (Ph.D. 1965) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Toronto (~1968–1977) and Oxford (1977–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha (1919–2002) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett (~1946–1948). He held posts at Patna College, Patna University (from 1958), and K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (attested 1971).
